title: Tohoku 2011 recorded on three components at fourteen GSN stations: the kinds of waves told apart by their motion, and the direction the P wave came from
verdict_rule: Flat would win if the direction the P wave arrives from, read off its own motion, matched the straight line to the epicentre on one flat map better than the great-circle direction.
license_note: GSN (network IU, Albuquerque Seismological Laboratory/USGS), open data from the EarthScope (ex-IRIS) data centre; cite the network DOI 10.7914/SN/IU.

sources.cite: Albuquerque Seismological Laboratory/USGS (2014), Global Seismograph Network (GSN - IRIS/USGS), International Federation of Digital Seismograph Networks, network IU
EarthScope Consortium, FDSN web services (station, dataselect)

units.traces: ground velocity over each station's peak (counts / channel scale)

inputs.origin: Our list of fourteen GSN stations.
EarthScope FDSN station service, channel metadata (orientation) of each station.
EarthScope FDSN dataselect, three components, 2011-03-11 05:41-08:16 UTC (and the other events' windows).

notes: Window 05:41-08:16 UTC on 2011-03-11 (data window only; no origin time or travel time is used in the analysis). Station latitudes and longitudes, and the ISC epicentre, enter only as angles. Sensor orientations come from the channel metadata.
